plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap (greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), consequential damages exclusion with direct-damage carve-outs, and an Excluded Claims definition covering confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP. Check cap size against playbook parameters and whether data-breach/indemnity carve-outs are uncapped; 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability.

Vendor IP indemnity in 20.1 and misconduct/data/law indemnity in 20.2; Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is narrow with carve-outs. 20.4 procedure and 20.5 infringement remedies (with refund on straight-line three-year basis) should be checked against preferred position; 9.3 cross-references 20.5.

12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to develop, buy or sell anything and disclaims non-compete/MFN/volume/no-hire commitments — beneficial to us. Confirm nothing in 2.2 (exclusivity) or elsewhere operates as a de facto non-compete; if it does, address under EXCLUSIVITY rather than double-flagging.

Sec-2.2 (first of two clauses numbered 2.2) makes Vendor Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the term — a direct hit on this rule and inconsistent with 12.3 and 2.1. Note the internal conflict when proposing deletion.

Sec-7.2 (first clause numbered 7.2) requires Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than its best terms with any technology supplier — MFN running against us. 12.3 disclaims any MFN commitment; flag the conflict and the direction.

Sec-12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars engagement as well as solicitation, and has no general-advertising carve-out. Compare with 12.3's general-recruitment freedom.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and Customer-specific cause termination rights (plus force-majeure exit in 27.3); no convenience termination on notice for Customer appears anywhere. Note the missing Section 9.4 gap in the numbering before concluding it is absent.

8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months on a one hundred eighty day non-renewal notice — test against the playbook's maximum notice window. 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and three percent with ninety days' notice, which likely satisfies the pricing limb; do not double-flag pricing.

New York law, no CISG, exclusive New York County courts with injunctive-relief carve-out and an executive escalation step — appears within accepted jurisdictions and court-based (no foreign arbitration). Verify escalation does not bar urgent relief.

24.1 gives Customer free affiliate/successor assignment; 24.2 restricts Vendor; 24.4 bars Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control. Confirm 24.3's residual consent requirement does not cut back 24.1 and that 13.3 licence transfer aligns.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP; 14.2 assigns Deliverables to Customer on creation subject to payment; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology with a perpetual licence back via 13.2. Check the definitions of Deliverable (1.4) and Vendor Technology (1.8) and the no-training restriction in 15.1 for any leakage of our rights.

13.1 covers Affiliates and contractors for internal business purposes; 13.2 grants a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered software/Vendor Technology; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured breach after notice and cure. Confirm 13.4 restrictions are not broader than acceptable.

Sec-22.1 lets Vendor audit at any time without notice with remote access to Customer systems — fails notice, frequency and off-site limbs. 22.2 (Vendor bears cost, no direct system access, five percent threshold) and 22.3 are protective; propose conforming 22.1 to them. Section 23 may also contain records/assurance obligations.

Sec-7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages on Customer for dependency delays — squarely against the rule's direction. Note interaction with the liability cap in 21.1 but flag only under this rule.

19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties; 19.2 gives ninety days for Deliverables and full-term conformity for hosted Services; 19.4 provides re-perform/repair/replace with refund fallback and is expressly non-exclusive for key claims. Check the ninety-day Deliverable period against the playbook's minimum duration; 19.5 disclaimer is mutual and preserves express remedies.

Section 18 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2,000,000 and cyber USD 5,000,000 with one year tail, certificates on request and no limitation of liability. Compare each limit to playbook minimums; additional-insured status may be absent but is likely a rationale note only.

2.1 expressly states no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining a further Order Form is not a breach; 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges and 12.3 disclaims minimum-volume commitments. Likely compliant; confirm no take-or-pay hides in the exclusivity clause at sec-2.2.

Section 11 provides up to six months' transition assistance at expiring rates, thirty-day return of Customer Data in machine-readable format with no fee-dispute hold-back, and certified deletion. 10.1–10.2 cover post-termination rights and refunds; 16.5 defers to Sections 11 and 15 for Customer Data.
